amendments.body: In `emit_molt_failure` (shrimp.rs ~line 1380-1381), the `critical_gh_failure` computation lacks the `params.gh_min_d > 0.0` guard that was added to `critical_gh_deficit` in `molt_cycle` (line 554-555). When `gh_min_d == 0.0` (user disables GH minimum), the event path computes `gh_ratio = 0/0.01 = 0` which falsely triggers `critical_gh_failure`, emitting a misleading "critical GH ratio 0.00<0.30" detail instead of the correct "score X<Y" form. Fix: add the same `params.gh_min_d > 0.0 &&` guard to line 1381, i.e. `let critical_gh_failure = params.gh_min_d > 0.0 && gh_ratio < params.critical_molt_gh_ratio;`
amendments.rationale: Diagnostic consistency bug. The event reporting path disagrees with the molt resolution path about whether a critical GH deficit occurred. This violates the acceptance criterion that events 'expose enough detail to explain why molt failure occurred' — it would explain a failure with a cause the simulation didn't actually use. The test `test_zero_ca_and_mg_min_parameters_use_defensive_guards` doesn't catch this because it asserts `last_molt_success == true` (the molt succeeds, so `emit_molt_failure` is never called). A test where `gh_min_d=0`, minerals are absent, and condition is poor enough to fail the molt would surface the misleading event.

payload.summary: Reviewed the 5-file diff introducing `temp_condition_min_factor` as a named parameter (replacing hardcoded 0.25), and adding a `gh_min_d > 0.0` guard to the `critical_gh_deficit` check in `molt_cycle`. The temp-factor refactor is clean: the old hardcoded floor is replaced with the species parameter everywhere (implementation, tests in events.rs and molt_mineral_budget.rs), validation accepts 0.0, and a defensive `.max(0.01)` epsilon prevents division-by-zero. The new test `test_temp_condition_min_factor_controls_molt_cadence_floor` correctly demonstrates that lowering the floor delays molt readiness under cold conditions. The zero-GH-minimum test correctly verifies that disabling mineral minimums doesn't trip the critical-GH hard-fail path. One real bug found: the `emit_molt_failure` event-reporting function computes its own `critical_gh_failure` flag without the new `gh_min_d > 0.0` guard, creating a diagnostic inconsistency where events blame "critical GH ratio" when the simulation itself did not treat the GH deficit as critical.
